texts: Mesenchymal stem cells, bone marrow cells (BMCs), endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) and skeletal myoblasts have all been used in clinical trials of cell therapy for heart disease: all of the above.
Skeletal myoblasts were tested in the MAGIC trial, bone marrow cells in BOOST and REPAIR-AMI, and mesenchymal stem cells in POSEIDON, among others.

In the picture, all four trays grow in the same scar: the messy heap (MESS-enchymal), the cracked bone (marrow), the seedlings that grow into tiny pipes (endothelial) and the tiny skeletons (skeletal myoblasts).
The benefits so far have been modest, and the cells seem to work mostly through the signals they release rather than by becoming new heart muscle.
Memory hook: all four trays have been planted in a scar.
